A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix B report original numerical simulations, convex toy experiments and SlimPajama training experiments with 124M/210M language models. These qualify independently of Figure 1a, which is attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds reported ImageNet and OpenWebText2 training results and numerical schedule-optimization results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The existing schedule-extension and learning-rate-transfer procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds an illustrative procedure that uses projected gradient descent with momentum to optimize every positive schedule value jointly, choosing both schedule shape and scale.

E1.justification: v2 adds ImageNet image classification and OpenWebText2 language modeling in Appendices C.1–C.2. This substantially extends the empirical coverage beyond the retained SlimPajama language-model experiments and convex toy problem.

E2.justification: The new schedule-optimization comparison in Figure 28 includes the analytical linear-decay bound and a PEPit linear-decay reference; v1's numerical PEP comparison in Figure 7 covers WSD and cosine. Existing comparisons are retained, while the added dataset experiments reuse established schedule families.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces substantial new evaluation settings: 100-epoch ResNet50 training with SGD and heavy-ball momentum, training loss and top-1 validation accuracy, and OpenWebText2 experiments with 60M/93M/166M models across multiple horizons. The original SlimPajama settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 and Figure 28 add a numerical analysis of whether optimizing the bound over the entire schedule recovers linear decay under constant gradient-norm bounds. Existing cooldown, gradient-norm, cosine-cycle, PEP and minimum-versus-last-iterate analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-seed aggregation, confidence intervals or significance tests for the training comparisons. The five-epoch running averages introduced for ImageNet smooth training curves; they do not report statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Figures 25–28 add ImageNet loss/accuracy and learning-rate-sweep results, OpenWebText2 curves across three model sizes, and convergence of numerical schedule optimization toward linear decay. These are additional results under new settings. The original plotted results and reported SlimPajama losses, including 2.9535 versus 2.9660 in Section 5.2, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the equality in v1 Theorem 9 to an upper-bound inequality in Theorem E.2 and corrects the harmonic-term labeling in Section 3.2. It removes Appendix F.2's approximate polynomial-decay derivation. The central WSD bound and mirror-descent analysis remain, with the full WSD statement relocated to Appendix G.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: convex last-iterate bounds resemble practical scheduling behavior, cooldown removes logarithmic dependence, and theory guides schedule extension and learning-rate transfer. The new experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 revises the transformer-only empirical limitation to acknowledge the added vision experiments. Appendix C explicitly cautions that multi-pass ImageNet validation metrics involve generalization effects and that numerical schedule optimization has limited practical applicability and no certified global optimum.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds implementation information: timm, ImageNet momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0001, batch size 4 × 256 and augmentation settings, plus PyTorch automatic differentiation and constant initialization for schedule optimization. Existing training details and access links are retained; OpenWebText2 training details are largely delegated to a cited work.

R1.justification: v2 adds He et al. (2016) for ResNet and Wightman (2019) for timm. The related-work arguments and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged. Publication and title updates for retained references do not constitute additional cited works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized tightening and caption edits. v2 replaces the detailed contents page with an appendix overview, adds an impact statement, and shortens the main WSD theorem while preserving its full statement in the appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, substantially resizing and relocating figures and equations. Figures 8 and 9 exchange positions, and Figures 25–28 are added. The original graphical results are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: Appendix C strengthens empirical support beyond v1's SlimPajama/AdamW model-training evidence through vision experiments with SGD and another language corpus. The numerical schedule analysis and corrected theorem inequality also help. These gains remain corroborative: the central theory-to-practice gap persists, and removing the polynomial-decay derivation reduces theoretical breadth. With the main results preserved, the net improvement is modest.
